items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 parameter count resolves to layered architecture — 552B MoE backbone + ~200B n-gram component ≈ 748B total; 763B is the full variant with vision + MTP; 512 GB unified memory is the real self-hosting threshold; gateway pricing still splits 2–4x on the same MIT-licensed model
items.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the Chinese open-weight anchor behind this week's cheap-agent-tier model comparisons, including the MiniMax M3.1 Flash launch coverage still carried in the pm (Automation-Bench 62.2 vs V4.1 Flash-1017 60.5; DeepSWE v1.1 73.7 vs V4.1 Flash-1017 77.0). Overnight searches resolve the parameter-count discrepancy flagged in yesterday's pm. Third-party aggregators listing 552B total / 16B active (Requesty, Gradually.ai, GetDeploying, DataLearner) are describing the Mixture-of-Experts backbone alone. The Hugging Face safetensors footprint reported by Neura News at ~748.5B — the figure that initially looked contradictory — is now corroborated by a second aggregator (getmaxim.ai) that explicitly describes the architecture as a 552B MoE backbone with an n-gram component of roughly 200B on top, i.e. 552B + ~200B ≈ 748B, and by a German report that puts the full model at 748B and says the full-quality version requires a 512 GB unified-memory machine. The 763B figure in the Hugging Face card is the V4.1-Flash-1017 revision, which adds vision and MTP (multi-token prediction) components on top of the 748B base; the French-language aiweekly.co coverage specifically cites 763B with MIT license and 42.6 on HLE without tools. Checkpoint size settles near the Neura News figure (~511.76 GB) once the n-gram component is counted. Gateway pricing still splits 2–4x on the same MIT-licensed model: Requesty $0.30 input / $1.20 output per million; another aggregator $0.15 / $0.60 off-peak; a third $0.22 / $0.66. Artificial Analysis anchor: Intelligence Index 40 at $0.27/task. The MIT license and Hugging Face publication remain the consistent facts across every source; the deepseek-ai Hugging Face model card is still the primary artifact for direct verification.
items.why_it_matters: The practical read on V4.1 Flash now has sharper numbers than yesterday. First, the self-hosting threshold is clearer: the figure that matters is 748B — the ~500 GB on-disk safetensors footprint, requiring roughly 512 GB unified memory for a full-quality run — not the 552B the aggregators lead with (which is only the MoE backbone). That is single-rig-with-serious-RAM territory, not laptop territory. Not Gabe's immediate problem — self-hosting a 500 GB checkpoint from a Python script is well off the beginner path — but the general lesson generalizes to every open-weight model: read the safetensors metadata on the Hugging Face card before planning around any third-party listing, because aggregators tend to repeat the vendor's backbone-only figure rather than count the add-on components. Second, the gateway pricing split is the one directly actionable fact. The same MIT-licensed model is 2–4x more expensive on one gateway than another for identical token traffic. For the 'cheap-and-measure on three real tasks' trial pattern this week's coverage keeps recommending (first against MiniMax M3.1 Flash, now against V4.1 Flash), pulling the exact Hugging Face model-ID string into the gateway's price list before scripting is the move that avoids a surprise. Third, the layered-architecture framing — MoE backbone + n-gram component + vision/MTP in the 1017 revision — is a useful mental model for the rest of the Chinese open-weight stack, which is likely to keep shipping with mixed components rather than a single parameter number.
items.why_it_matters_brief: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's parameter discrepancy resolves: 552B MoE backbone + ~200B n-gram ≈ 748B total — the first clear look at how Chinese open-weight models stack layered components under one headline number.

revisions.change: created — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 is the Chinese open-weight benchmark anchor behind the MiniMax M3.1 Flash launch coverage currently in the am. Parameter count across listings: 552B total / 16B active on Requesty, Gradually.ai, GetDeploying, DataLearner — but Neura News reports Hugging Face safetensors show ~748.5B for backbone + engram and ~763B including MTP + vision, with a Reddit thread cited as arguing the real total is 748B not 552B. Checkpoint size: ~314 GB at 4-bit (one aggregator) vs ~511.76 GB (Neura News). Pricing split across gateways: Requesty $0.30/$1.20 per M input/output; another aggregator $0.15/$0.60 off-peak; a third $0.22/$0.66 — ~2-4x spread. Benchmark reads: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 40 at $0.27/task; Requesty Intelligence Index 39.5%. MIT license and Hugging Face publication are consistent across every source. DNS to huggingface.co, deepseek.com, and primary benchmark pages all failed from this run's environment — relied on WebSearch summaries across ~16 queries. hero_image set to null.

resolved the parameter-count discrepancy with a second corroborating source (getmaxim.ai) that describes the architecture explicitly as a 552B MoE backbone plus a ~200B n-gram component, matching the Neura News safetensors figure (~748.5B) and the German report of 748B total requiring a 512 GB unified-memory machine for full-quality. The 763B figure in the HF card is the V4.1-Flash-1017 revision which adds vision + MTP on top of the 748B base; aiweekly.co confirms 763B MIT with 42.6 HLE no-tools. Updated summary to lead with the layered-architecture resolution; rewrote why_it_matters around the clearer self-hosting threshold (512 GB RAM, not 300 GB) and the aggregator vs safetensors reading lesson; rewrote why_it_matters_brief with the layered-component framing. Gateway pricing split and MIT license facts unchanged. No late-breaking Tier-1 items added — strict 12-hour window from 2026-10-20T18:00Z surfaced nothing from Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, Meta, Mistral, Alibaba Qwen, or Hugging Face trackers. Mistral Large 4 open-weights release is now confirmed for Oct 27 but outside the 12-hour window.

takes.source: Neura News — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: 1M context, MIT license, 763B parameters
takes.take: The parameter-count-discrepancy source. Reports that Hugging Face safetensors show ~748.5B parameters for backbone + engram, and that including the MTP and vision components brings the total closer to 763B. Also lists checkpoint size at ~511.76 GB and references a Reddit thread arguing the real total is 748B not 552B. Overnight corroboration from getmaxim.ai (552B MoE + ~200B n-gram breakdown) and from the German pasqualepillitteri.it (748B total requiring 512 GB unified memory) now resolves this against the aggregators.

takes.source: getmaxim.ai — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model comparison page
takes.take: The architectural-breakdown source added by enrichment. Describes V4.1 Flash as a 552B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with roughly 8B parameters active for input and 16B for output, with a separate n-gram component of roughly 200B on top of the MoE backbone. This directly explains why aggregator figures (552B, MoE-only) and Hugging Face safetensors figures (~748.5B, backbone + n-gram) differ by exactly the n-gram component size.

takes.source: aiweekly.co (FR) — DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 : 763B sous MIT, 42,6 sur HLE sans outils
takes.take: French-language anchor on the 1017 revision. Confirms 763B parameters under MIT license, cites the Hugging Face model card, and reports a Humanity's Last Exam score of 42.6 without tools. The 763B figure is the full 1017 revision (vision + MTP added on top of the 748B base), consistent with Neura News.

takes.source: pasqualepillitteri.it (DE) — DeepSeek veröffentlicht V4.1 Flash, einen 748-Milliarden-Flash der jetzt sieht
takes.take: Secondary 748B anchor. Puts the full model at 748 billion parameters and notes the full-quality version requires a 512 GB unified-memory machine for self-hosting. This is the practical hardware threshold line that lets Gabe calibrate the gap between 'runnable on consumer hardware' (not this model) and 'hostable on a single-rig setup' (yes, if the rig has 512 GB RAM).

takes.source: Requesty — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page
takes.take: Lists 552B total / 16B active parameters, MIT license, 1M context, Requesty Intelligence Index 39.5%. Pricing listed at $0.30 input / $1.20 output per million tokens. Representative of the backbone-only parameter figure that most third-party aggregators carry — the figure that is correct for 'MoE backbone' but incorrect as a total.

takes.source: GetDeploying — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash llm listing
takes.take: Open weights, MIT license. Lists provider pricing in the $0.15 input / $0.60 output off-peak bracket — the same tier MiniMax M3.1 Flash is being quoted at this week. Confirms the 2-4x gateway pricing split against Requesty's $0.30 / $1.20 for identical traffic on the same MIT-licensed model.

takes.source: DataLearner — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash analysis page
takes.take: Independent coding-benchmark anchor. Ranks V4.1 Flash first on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (90.6) and first on CodeForces (3471) among 21 tracked models; DeepSWE 74.2 places it second of 38. Note that this is Terminal-Bench 2.1, a different version than Terminal-Bench 4.0 cited in MiniMax M3.1 Flash's launch table (38.1) — direct cross-reads between the two Chinese models on terminal-coding workloads are not clean.

takes.source: Artificial Analysis — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page
takes.take: Independent anchor. Intelligence Index 40 at $0.27/task. Vals ranks V4.1 Flash the top open-weight model on its index, per Neura News's secondary citation. The $0.27/task figure is the one that lets a cheap-and-measure trial from a Python script be budgeted directly against MiniMax M3.1 Flash's roughly comparable $0.15/$0.60 bracket.
